memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When the Lord your God brings you into the land you are entering to possess and drives out before you many nations—the Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, seven nations larger and stronger than you—and when the Lord your God has delivered them over to you and you have defeated them, then you must destroy them totally. Make no treaty with them, and show them no mercy. - Deut 7:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
We cannot read these verses honestly without feeling their weight. God commands Israel to completely destroy the nations of Canaan and show no mercy. This is one of the hard passages of Scripture, and it would be wrong to soften it into something comfortable. We must let it sit in its own historical and covenant setting rather than treating it as a general pattern for how God's people act in every age.

Several things help us understand it. This was a specific, one-time command tied to a particular moment in God's redemptive plan — the judgment of nations whose wickedness, including child sacrifice and deep corruption, had reached its full measure (Gen 15:16). It was not a license for ethnic hatred but an act of divine judgment carried out through Israel, and a protection against the spiritual corruption that would destroy Israel's faith. God takes sin with deadly seriousness.

We should be careful never to use texts like this to justify violence today. This command belonged to that unique covenant moment and is not repeated for the church. Under the new covenant, Jesus tells us our battle is not against flesh and blood, and He sends us not to destroy enemies but to love them and call them to repentance (Matt 5:44; Eph 6:12). The seriousness of God's judgment here should drive us to the cross, where judgment and mercy meet, and where we find refuge from the wrath our own sin deserves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- How do I respond to the difficult passages of Scripture — do I face them honestly?
- What does this text teach me about how seriously God takes sin?
- How does the cross help me hold together God's judgment and His mercy?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, some of Your Word is hard, and I do not always understand Your ways. Help me to trust Your justice and Your goodness, to take sin seriously, and to run to the cross where Your judgment and mercy meet. Amen.
